hero.heading: Copper Mountain Technologies, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built September 25, 2026, from coppermountaintech.com and its public price pages, the Conexus Indiana case study, and federal data. Every number is labeled: published, federal, or our assumption. The assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: Exact computed endpoints: $54,775.00 and $268,800.00, rounded to the nearest $5,000 for display.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Analyzers you ship in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per hundred analyzers.

sliders.label: Engineering hours that ship free with each analyzer, first year
Loaded cost of one engineering hour
Posted price of a representative analyzer, inside your printed anchors
Materials share of a posted price
Months a posted price stands while input costs move

constants.text: The federal producer price index for electronic components rose 26.5 percent from October 2025 to August 2026 [[BENCHMARK]], BLS series WPU1178. This one is not a slider.

model.formulaText: Moved per 100 analyzers = 100 × free hours × loaded rate + 100 × posted price × materials share × 0.265 × (months / 12)
model.plainText: In words, the engineering hours that ship free with each analyzer at their loaded cost, plus the slice of this year's component-price rise a posted price absorbs while it stands.
model.callout: You publish your prices. Nobody in this trade publishes the engineering hours that ship free with every analyzer sold. If those hours are your differentiator, they deserve a price tag, or a proof that zero is the right one.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: Your store is labeled a public price list, and your product pages print their prices: $9,995.00, $10,495.00, $15,995.00 [[OBSERVED]].
Your software ships with every feature included, at no additional cost, in your own words [[OBSERVED]].
You publish refurbished prices to the cent and your calibration services pricing [[OBSERVED]].
Your V0602 page says it replaced the M5065 at the same posted price, with better specifications [[OBSERVED]].
By your own account, it took your largest competitor, a global company, seven years to answer your form factor [[OBSERVED]].
In February 2024 one of your analyzers measured fuel inside a lunar lander's tanks on the way to the Moon; NASA published the paper [[BENCHMARK]].
